account:
Today I have my usual mayoral appointments, including the ten o'clock mill grain inspection, and an added eighteen-hundred great hall lighting inspection with the builder. The secretary is keeping the appointment records and has prepared a grain enquiry report. I have read it and should return it before we leave for the mill. Grain stock and delivery terms still need confirming; no public purchase has been authorized.

There is unusually elaborate activity around tonight's hall inspection. The baker and innkeeper were at the hall early this morning. The baker says two hundred 'jubilee' loaves are ready, and freight is helping deliver them into the great hall table chests. Freight said he had deposited 160 loaves and thought the baker might have delivered another 32. I have not checked those quantities myself. The innkeeper specified the four table chests, asked me again to attend at eighteen, and said we would discuss the account privately afterward. He describes the bread as his own commission for an inn hospitality arrangement and says he will settle the baker's account. Earlier, freight personally supplied the baker with 24 emeralds and 72 wheat toward this order; the report says another 528 wheat was needed then. This is a particular commission, not evidence of a standing daily bread requirement.

Two hundred jubilee loaves seem excessive for merely inspecting lights. My questions about whose jubilee this is have not received a clear answer. The repeated efforts to secure my attendance, the hall preparations, and the word 'jubilee' make me suspect a celebration or gathering is being arranged under cover of the lighting inspection, perhaps meant as a surprise. I do not know whom or what it celebrates, or whether it is intended for me. The baker, freight, and innkeeper are plainly involved in provisioning; the builder is associated with the lighting, and the secretary with scheduling. I cannot conclude that all of them know a hidden purpose. For now I will keep my appointments, learn what I can directly, and keep this private bread arrangement separate from treasury spending.
